## Primary correction r2 — frozen candidate

Independent reviewer finding on r1: requiring a unique row in `State::source_drain_completions` changed accepted observations and made `MissingUseRoot` depend on an auxiliary table that may omit a row under allocation pressure. R57's actual `Native.completed` projection is derived from the Origin's inline Drain record and does not contain this side table. The r1 check was removed before integration.

The proof author independently uses the exact R57 model: selected indexed Origin, inline Drain record, occurrence/slot/cause/task endpoints, created/selected relation, empty incoming/replay, and `completed=true`. The primary correction therefore removes only the completion-table index/pointer/uniqueness requirement. It retains the existing unique source-Origin lookup and ancestry operation, and carries the already-selected Origin index/reference plus its inline drain receipt through the owner projection. No second root search, changed inference/routing/subtraction operation, new failure variant, or compiled/runtime claim is introduced.

The Rust author stopped because remaining time against the original 1,000-second lane budget could not be established; no r2 author edits occurred. The primary accepted the exact stopped-path handoff and made this bounded correction under the existing primary closeout envelope. No budget was reset or increased.

## R2 review closeout and primary warning repair

The independent R2 source review found no blocking or major correctness issue. It confirmed that removing the r1 completion-table scan restores baseline acceptance/failure precedence and that the retained Origin, occurrence, inline drain receipt, cause, task and relation checks match the R57 finite-record model. Two minor items remained: the borrowed `source_drain` binding was unused, and the proof handoff's anticipated signatures were truncated. The review did not run a compiler or certify Rust compilation/runtime.

The unused-binding warning is repaired by using the bound receipt directly in the pointer association guard (`std::ptr::eq(source_drain, self.entry.source_drain)`). This is behavior-preserving: the binding already came from that Origin's `source_drain_receipt`; the guard now checks that exact borrowed value without rereading the Option. `git diff --check` passes on the exact receiver path. No Rust compiler, Cargo, tests, build, formatter, or Lean command was run for this repair.
